entities.text: High Court Of Kerala At Ernakulam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The petitioner is the 2nd accused in C.C. No.18 of 2018 on the file of the Court of the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Kottayam, for allegedly committing the offences punishable under Sections 403, 406,
468, 472, 420 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
2. The Trial Court had enlarged the petitioner on bail, subject to the condition that she should surrender her passport.
Subsequently, by Annexure-A1 order, this Court deleted the condition in the bail order and permitted the petitioner to go abroad for a period of two months from 14.07.2025.
This Court also observed that the petitioner can participate in trial by availing the video linkage facility as provided under the Electronic Video Linkage Rules for Courts (Kerala), 2021.

entities.text: Electronic Video Linkage Rules for Courts (Kerala), 2021
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
However,
the petitioner could not return to India due to circumstances beyond her control.
Consequently, she filed an application before the Trial Court to avail the video linkage facility.
But, by Annexure-A2 order, the Trial Court dismissed the application, in view of the specific condition imposed by this Court in Annexure-A1 order.
Assailing Annexure-A2 order, the petitioner filed Crl.M.C. No.9260/2025.

By Annexure-A3 order,
this Court finding that there was no illegality in Annexure-A2 order, dismissed the Crl.M.C.
3.

The petitioner contends that, it is only due to circumstances beyond her control and on the risk of her losing her employment, that she is unable to return to India, as stipulated in Annexure-A1 order.
The petitioner undertakes that she would return to India on or before 31.12.2025.
Moreover, the case is posted for the prosecution evidence.

Non bailable warrants have been issued against CWs 21,
23 and 24.
Without procuring their presence, the trial in this case will not progress.
Therefore, the petitioner's personal appearance before the Trial Court is actually unnecessary.
The petitioner does not have any CRL.MC NO. 9716 OF 2025 4 2025:KER:85003 intention to flee from justice.

Hence,
the petitioner may be granted a breathing time to appear before the Trial Court till 31.12.2025.
In the meantime the petitioner may avail the electronic video linkage as permitted in Annexure-A1 order.

5. Heard; the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.
6.
By Annexure-A1 order, this Court permitted the petitioner to go abroad for a period of two months from 14.07.2025.
It is not in dispute that the petitioner did not return back to India within the stipulated time period.

She also did not file an application before the Trial Court within the Renju P. George vs State Of Kerala on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82721530/
2 stipulated time period for availing the electronic video linkage.

entities.text: Renju P. George vs State Of Kerala
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is after the lapse of the time period that she filed the application, which was rejected by the Trial Court on the ground that the petitioner has to first surrender before the Trial Court and then file the application.
It was in the said circumstances this Court also upheld Annexure-A2 order.

7. Now the petitioner has filed this Crl.M.C. for an extension of the time period of Annexure-A1 order for both CRL.MC NO. 9716 OF 2025 5 2025:KER:85003 surrendering before the Trial Court and also availing the video linkage facility.

8. Taking into consideration the fact that the case is only posted for prosecution evidence and that non bailable warrants have been issued against the court witnesses, I don't find any necessity for the petitioner's personal appearance before the Trial Court.

9. In Abhil C.R. v. State of Kerala [2025 KHC OnLine 1650], Sathisan v. State of Kerala [2025 KHC 2154] and Rameshan v. State of Kerala [2025 (6) KHC 545], this Court has succinctly held that an accused person can very well avail the electronic video linkage facility even for the questioning under Section 351 of the BNSS, corresponding to Section 313 of Cr.P.C.
10.

sentences.text: In the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case, I am inclined to extend the time period fixed in Annexure-A1 order till 31.12.2025, and permit the petitioner to file an application to avail the electronic video linkage.
In the aforesaid circumstances, I allow the Crl.M.C., CRL.MC NO. 9716 OF 2025 6 2025:KER:85003 by extending the time period fixed in Annexure-A1 order till 31.12.2025.

In the meantime, it would be upto the petitioner to avail the electronic video linkage facility as provided under the Electronic Video Linkage Rules for Courts (Kerala), 2021 and the law referred to the aforesaid decisions through her counsel, but by specifically undertaking that she will not dispute her identity and appear before the Trial Court, as and when her presence is absolutely imperative.

entities.text: Electronic Video Linkage Rules for Courts (Kerala), 2021
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: If such an application is filed, the Trial Court shall compassionately consider the application and pass orders thereon.
The Crl.M.C. is ordered accordingly.
